passages.context: The Beatitudes and The Sermon on The Mount
St. Paul on spiritual combat and the promise of future glory.

passages.message: Letting go of anxiety and instead praying to God and trusting in Him. God's peace surpasses all understanding.
passages.context: St. Paul's exhorations to the Phillipians.

passages.message: The Mirror that is the Law
passages.context: St. Paul on the doctrine of salvation.

passages.message: A recognition of God's supremacy and His goodness. A person should not be followed as God is and divisions should not be spread because one person is evangelized by one instead of another. Rather, everyone should follow God in the best way possible, not simply the people who led them to Him.
passages.context: People in Corinth who caused divisions by claiming to follow preachers rather than the One whom they were preaching.

passages.message: God's love ifor us is so great that He gave up even His Son for us.
passages.context: A summary of God's love and plan given to by Jesus to Nicodemus

passages.message: Beware so as not to believe that you are responsible for your blessings, for even the power that you used to obtain them has been given to you.
passages.context: A warning not to forget God in good times

passages.message: God brings good out of all things, even the evil of others. See Romans 8:28.
passages.context: Joseph comforts his brothers as they ask him for forgiiveness for the evil they did to him.

passages.message: The 10 Commandments - The core commandments of God's moral law.
passages.context: Moses gives the 10 Commandments at Mount Sinai.

passages.message: Part of the shema for the jewish people and one of the two most important commandments according to Jesus.
passages.context: Moses warns the people of Israel to remain faithful and advises them as to how before entering the promised land.

passages.message: God looks at a man's heart, not his appearances and therefore you should too. In the same way, do not judge people, for you cannot see what is in their hearts.
passages.context: God tells Samuel who from Jesse's house to appoint as king.

passages.message: All that you have you have received. You are not entitled to it. The Lord gives and He takes away, and in doing so does no wrong. Be grateful therefore for what you have and don't take it for granted. Know most of all that you will surely lose it all one day at your death.
passages.context: Job reacts after having lost all his property and his children.

passages.message: The book of Judges is not an instruction book on how to live, nor a book of praise for those in it, but rather a warning to all those who read it: act according to what is right.
passages.context: The end of the book of Judges, after the terrible story of the Benjaminites at Gibeah and Israel's subsequent actions.
